cli.about: Majordomus control plane: a data-driven MCP server over the repository's .ai/ layer
cli.long_about:
The Rust executable of Majordomus. It reads the repository's provider-neutral AI layer under .ai/ and serves it, read-only, to MCP clients over stdio.

The task lifecycle (init, start, check, finish, doctor, ...) is the shell tool bin/majordomus in the same repository; this executable does not implement those commands.

args.name: discovery

possible_values.name: filesystem

args.name: inspect
args.help: Print what would be served, and every diagnostic, then exit without serving

args.name: format
args.help: Output shape of --inspect

possible_values.name: text
possible_values.help: Lines for a person

possible_values.name: json
possible_values.help: One JSON document, deterministic

args.help: The transport to serve on

possible_values.name: stdio

args.name: standalone
args.help: Serve this client alone: no shared server, no HTTP, no Swagger UI, no peers, and nothing written anywhere. The default is the shared server (below)

args.name: http_host
args.help: Interface the shared server binds when this process is the one that starts it

args.name: http_port
args.help: Port the shared server binds when this process starts it; when it is taken, a free port is used instead and the URL is logged on stderr either way

examples.title: See what would be served, without serving it
examples.description: Builds the registry and the index of the repository in the working directory and prints the repository, the capabilities, the objects and every diagnostic, then exits. Nothing is served and nothing is written.

examples.title: The same, as one JSON document for a script
examples.description: The shape `--inspect` prints for a person, as JSON: the repository, its discovery mode, the capabilities and the diagnostics, deterministic and safe to diff.
examples.expectation: exits 0; prints one JSON document carrying /repository/repository/root, /tools

examples.title: Serve one MCP client on stdio
examples.description: The form an MCP client spawns: JSON-RPC frames in on stdin, frames out on stdout, logs on stderr, and the session ends at end of input. `--standalone` keeps this process to itself: no shared server, no HTTP, nothing written anywhere.
examples.expectation: answers initialize and tools/list on stdio, and exits 0 at end of input
